questions.question: What is the purpose of an exception rule in Vulnerability Response?

options.text: To automatically request an exception for VIs matching specific conditions

explanation.correct: An exception rule automatically requests an exception for a specific condition for a group of vulnerable items (VIs), such as a rule with a condition based on vulnerability severity. With this rule, you can defer new and existing VIs automatically if they match the approved rule condition.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Exception rules defer VIs, they don't delete them
Exception rules manage deferrals, not scanner integrations
Reports are generated by Performance Analytics, not exception rules

source.excerpt: Create a rule to automatically request an exception for a specific condition for a group of vulnerable items (VIs), such as a rule with a condition that is based on the vulnerability severity of these VIs.

subtopics: Handling vulnerability exceptions and false positives

questions.question: What role is required to create an exception rule in Vulnerability Response?

explanation.correct: The role required to create an exception rule is sn_vul.vulnerability_admin.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Remediation owners work on tasks, not exception rule creation
Vulnerability analysts can view and work with VITs but not create exception rules
vulnerability_read provides read access only

subtopics: Handling vulnerability exceptions and false positives

questions.question: What happens when an exception rule is approved?

options.text: All matching VIs are immediately closed
A remediation task is created in the Deferred state
The rule is deleted from the system
A change request is automatically created

explanation.correct: The remediation task (VUL) is created when the rule is approved. The grouping method for this VUL is known as exception rules. The VUL is created in the Deferred state.

wrongAnswers.explanation: VIs are deferred, not closed, when an exception rule is approved
The rule remains active to continue deferring matching VIs until expiration
A remediation task in Deferred state is created, not a change request

source.excerpt: The remediation task (VUL) is created when the rule is approved. The grouping method for this VUL is known as exception rules. The VUL is created in the Deferred state.

subtopics: Handling vulnerability exceptions and false positives

questions.question: Which fields define the time period during which an exception rule is active? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: The 'Valid from' field defines the date from which the rule is active to defer VIs, and 'Valid to' defines the date from which the remediation task stops accepting new VIs.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The field is called 'Valid from', not 'Start date'
The field is called 'Valid to', not 'End date'

source.excerpt: Valid from: Date from which this rule is active to defer the VIs. Valid to: Date from which the remediation task stops accepting new VIs.

subtopics: Handling vulnerability exceptions and false positives

questions.question: What happens when an exception rule is rejected?

options.text: The rule can be reopened in Draft state, updated, and resubmitted
All associated VIs are immediately closed
The rule is archived and cannot be modified

explanation.correct: If the rule is rejected, you can reopen it in the Draft state, update it, and then resubmit it for approval.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Rejected rules can be reopened and resubmitted, not permanently deleted
VIs are not affected by rule rejection; the rule simply doesn't take effect
Rejected rules can be reopened and modified, not archived

source.excerpt: If the rule is rejected, you can reopen it in the Draft state, update it, and then resubmit it for approval.

subtopics: Handling vulnerability exceptions and false positives

questions.question: What is the 'Deferred until' field used for in an exception rule?

options.text: The date when the rule becomes active
The date until when VULs and VIs are deferred; after this date the VUL closes and VIs are regrouped
The date when the rule was created
The date when email notifications are sent

explanation.correct: The 'Deferred until' field specifies the date until when VULs and VIs are deferred. On this date, the created VUL is closed, all the VIs move out of the group, and group rules are reapplied.

wrongAnswers.explanation: 'Valid from' specifies when the rule becomes active, not 'Deferred until'
'Deferred until' is when deferral ends, not when the rule was created
Email notifications are triggered at workflow stages, not based on 'Deferred until'

source.excerpt: Deferred until: Date until when the VULs and VIs are deferred. On this date, the created VUL is closed, all the VIs move out of the group, and group rules are reapplied.

subtopics: Handling vulnerability exceptions and false positives

questions.question: What option enables an exception rule to run on existing VIs the first time it executes?

explanation.correct: The 'Execute on existing data' option enables you to run the exception rule on existing data the first time that the rule is run.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The option is called 'Execute on existing data', not 'Apply retroactively'
The option is 'Execute on existing data', not 'Include historical VIs'
'Backfill mode' is not the correct option name

source.excerpt: Execute on existing data: Option that enables you to run this rule on existing data the first time that this rule is run.

subtopics: Handling vulnerability exceptions and false positives

questions.question:
Which statements about exception rule email notifications are true?
a) Email notifications are sent at every stage of the exception rule workflow
b) The requester receives an email when an exception rule is submitted
c) Email notifications are only sent when the rule is rejected
d) Emails provide the status and other details of the request

explanation.correct: Statements a, b, and d are true. Email notifications are sent at every workflow stage, including when submitted (requester gets confirmation). They provide status and details. Statement c is false - notifications are sent at all stages, not only rejection.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement c is false - notifications are sent at all stages, not just rejection
Statements a and d are also true, and c is false
Statements b and d are also true

source.excerpt: Email notifications are sent at every stage of the exception rule workflow. These emails provide the status and other details of a request. For example, when an exception rule is requested, the requester receives an email that confirms that the request is submitted.

questions.question: What system property must be enabled to automatically reevaluate and regroup VIs when assignment rules change?

explanation.correct: When an assignment group on an assignment rule changes, the vulnerable items can be automatically reevaluated and regrouped by enabling the system property sn_vul.rerun_task_rules.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The property is sn_vul.rerun_task_rules, not sn_vul.auto_regroup
The property is sn_vul.rerun_task_rules, not sn_vul.assignment_refresh
The property is sn_vul.rerun_task_rules, not sn_vul.rule_evaluation

source.excerpt: When an assignment group on an assignment rule changes, the vulnerable items can be automatically reevaluated and regrouped by enabling the system property sn_vul.rerun_task_rules

questions.question: What business rule must be activated to automate the regrouping of vulnerable items when assignment rules change?

explanation.correct: To automate the regrouping of vulnerable items, you must activate the business rule 'Link to Remediation Tasks'. When enabled, it regroups VIs by moving them to the relevant group or creating a group if needed.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The business rule is called 'Link to Remediation Tasks', not 'Regroup Vulnerable Items'
The business rule is 'Link to Remediation Tasks', not 'Auto-assign VIs'
The business rule is 'Link to Remediation Tasks', not 'Update Task Groups'

source.excerpt: To automate the regrouping of vulnerable items, you must activate the business rule Link Remediation Tasks. The business rule on being enabled, regroups the vulnerable items by moving them to the relevant group or by creating a group if they can't be grouped under any existing group.

questions.question: Which is NOT true about automated regrouping when the 'Link to Remediation Tasks' business rule is enabled?

options.text: VIs are removed from groups without deleting the groups
Only items created using remediation task rules or remediation effort are removed
Regrouping occurs when assignment groups are manually changed
Regrouping is done automatically when assignment group changes as part of an assignment rule

explanation.correct: Regrouping is done automatically ONLY when the assignment group changes as part of an assignment rule, NOT when it is manually changed. Manual changes do not trigger automatic regrouping.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is true - VIs are removed from groups without deleting the groups themselves
This is true - only items from remediation task rules or effort are affected
This is true - automatic regrouping happens on rule-based assignment changes

source.excerpt: Regrouping is done automatically only when the assignment group changes as part of an assignment rule and not when it is manually changed.

questions.question: A vulnerability admin needs to track deferrals that have been applied multiple times to identify potential exceptions that need permanent resolution. Which VR feature should they use?

options.text: Multiple deferrals module showing deferral counts

explanation.correct: The set deferral counts scheduled job runs daily to post counts for records deferred more than once in the Deferral count column. Records are displayed in the Multiple deferrals modules for VR, AVR, and CVR.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Multiple deferrals module specifically tracks repeated deferrals with counts
Vulnerability reports provide general metrics, not specific deferral tracking
Change request history tracks changes, not vulnerability deferrals

source.excerpt: Track the number of times a vulnerable item, application vulnerable item, container vulnerable item, or remediation task is deferred. The set deferral counts scheduled job runs daily to post counts for the records that are deferred more than once in the Deferral count column.

subtopics: Handling vulnerability exceptions and false positives

questions.question: How many vulnerability calculators are included in the Vulnerability Response base system?

explanation.correct: The Vulnerability Response base system includes two vulnerability calculators: Default Risk Calculator and Vulnerability Severity.

wrongAnswers.explanation: There are two calculators in the base system, not one
The base system includes two, not three
Only two calculators are included in the base system

source.excerpt: The Vulnerability Response base system includes two vulnerability calculators: Default Risk Calculator and Vulnerability Severity.

questions.question: What happens when multiple vulnerability calculators target the same field (Risk Score)?

options.text: Both calculators run and the highest score is used
All calculators run and scores are averaged
Only one calculator per target field can be active at a time
The calculators run in sequence and each modifies the result

explanation.correct: Only one calculator per target field (Risk Score) can be active at a time. The Vulnerability Severity calculator is disabled by default.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Only one calculator can be active per target field
Scores are not averaged; only one calculator can be active
Only one calculator is active at a time; they do not run in sequence

source.excerpt: Only one calculator per target field (Risk Score) can be active at a time.

questions.question: What is the default state of the Vulnerability Severity calculator in the base system?

explanation.correct: The Vulnerability Severity calculator is disabled by default in the Vulnerability Response base system.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Vulnerability Severity calculator is disabled by default
It is fully disabled by default, not partially active
It is disabled by default regardless of UI

source.excerpt: Vulnerability Severity is disabled by default.

questions.question: What information is recorded in the Notes section when a risk score is updated on a vulnerable item?

options.text: Only the new risk score value
The calculator group name and details of the update
The name of the user who triggered the recalculation
Only the timestamp of the change

explanation.correct: Whenever the risk score is updated on a VIT, the Notes section is updated with the calculator group name and other update details.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Notes section includes more detail than just the score value
The system records calculator group name, not just the user name
More than just the timestamp is recorded; calculator group name is included

source.excerpt: The Notes section is updated with the Calculator group name.

questions.question: An organization determines that external-facing CIs require higher risk scores. Which approach should they use in Vulnerability Response?

options.text: Manually update the risk score on each vulnerable item
Create a custom vulnerability calculator using CMDB CI attributes like Internet Facing
Request the vulnerability scanner to increase severity ratings
Change the CVSS score in the NVD database

explanation.correct: You can use attributes like Internet Facing from the CMDB CI configuration_item table to create logic for vulnerability risk calculators that assign higher risk scores to external-facing CIs.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Manual updates are inefficient; calculators automate this based on CI attributes
Scanner severity is separate from VR risk score calculation
NVD CVSS scores cannot be changed by the organization

source.excerpt: Use attributes such as Internet Facing for CIs to create logic for Vulnerability Response risk calculators.

questions.question: How does the Automatically update related vulnerable items feature work in remediation tasks?

options.text: It manually adds all new VIs to every open task
New VIs matching the task filter criteria are automatically added, and non-matching VIs are automatically removed
It only adds new VIs but never removes existing ones
It runs once daily to update all tasks

explanation.correct: When the 'Automatically update related vulnerable items' checkbox is selected, new VIs matching the filter criteria are automatically added, and VIs no longer matching are automatically removed.

wrongAnswers.explanation: It uses filter criteria, not indiscriminate addition to all tasks
VIs that no longer match are automatically removed as well
It operates in real-time based on filter criteria changes, not just daily

source.excerpt: New VIs matching the remediation task filter criteria are automatically added. VIs that no longer match are automatically removed.
